assurance.label: bounded
assurance.claim_scope_statement: Loom-style bounded schedule exploration under the bounds in this document is systematic concurrency testing, never proof. No claim in this document may be labeled above bounded. The companion connection model (assurance/formal/connection-model.tla) is capped at proved-model for the model only and establishes nothing about production Rust without a reviewed composition/refinement link.

provenance.census_method: Direct reads of the pinned quarantined tree. Every citation in this document is package-root-relative File.java:start[-end], was verified by reading the cited lines in-session, and is mechanically re-resolved (file exists, lines within bounds) by internal/formalplan whenever the quarantine tree is materialized.

us005_calibration.close_code_mutant_summary: jm-close-code-1000 (Java behavioral mutant) executed the full 258-scenario sweep in-sandbox and was killed 71 times (19+26+26 across tiers) against the predicted JAVA_INVALID_DATA close-code signature; jm-utf8-accept was killed 10 times on the 1007 scenarios; reruns byte-identical. Evidence scope, stated precisely: the mutant rewrites only OracleEngine's InvalidDataException catch to report 1000, so its kills live-confirm that the rejection-path close codes the runtime emits (1002/1007/1009 per scenario) are distinguishable from 1000 -- and nothing else. The kills do NOT exercise the empty-payload accept path (an empty close is accepted by setPayload and never enters the rewritten catch); the connection model's empty -> 1000 entry rests on the direct source read of CloseFrame.setPayload (framing/CloseFrame.java:250-251).

seams.name: WebSocketImpl.synchronizeWriteObject
seams.note: Makes the multi-buffer enqueue of one message's frames atomic against other senders: wire order of frames within a message and non-interleaving of messages are peer-observable.
seams.rust_mapping: Vacuous by construction: one SendText/SendBinary command is applied atomically by the single owner, which emits all of that command's write buffers before the next command. Plan invariant: committed writes of one command are contiguous.

seams.name: WebSocketImpl instance monitor (close/closeConnection/flushAndClose)
seams.note: The de-facto connection lock. Close INITIATION is only narrowly latch-protected: flushAndClose's stored close triple and the onWebsocketClosing delivery are guarded by the flushandclosestate latch (584-606), but close() sets CLOSING only AFTER flushAndClose returns (463-507), and onWebsocketClosing runs while readyState is still OPEN — so a listener re-entering close() from inside onWebsocketClosing can send a second close frame before the latch guard is reached: close-frame sending is NOT exactly-once under callback re-entry. Terminal delivery is likewise NOT exactly-once: onWebsocketClose fires at 557 BEFORE CLOSED is set at 566 under the reentrant monitor (530), so a re-entering listener receives a second terminal callback — at-least-once delivery (proof-targets target.formal.close.terminal-absorbing); the monitor gives single delivery only across threads and for non-reentrant listeners.
seams.rust_mapping: The owner's serialized state machine; transitions are idempotent commands and the terminal event is planned to be emitted exactly once by construction (US-017 AC2) — a port-side strengthening over shipped Java's at-least-once reentrant delivery, recorded as note.close.exactly-once-terminal-delivery in assurance/formal/proof-targets.json and pending its behavior-delta ledger entry (US-009).

seams.name: Draft_6455.byteBufferList monitor
seams.note: Decode is single-threaded per connection (Q2/Q4 pinning), so the lock defends a cross-thread reader the shipped threading never creates. The observable reassembly semantics including the checkBufferLimit cap (drafts/Draft_6455.java:1101-1108) are sequential logic.
seams.rust_mapping: Plain owned Vec<Bytes> inside ConnectionCore's bounded state; no lock.

seams.name: AbstractWebSocket.syncConnectionLost
seams.note: Guards keepalive timer configuration and checker-service lifecycle; heartbeat is adapter-side wall-clock behavior and ConnectionCore stays clock-free.
seams.rust_mapping: Adapter timer task issues Ping commands and an abnormal-close command on pong timeout; its own config is guarded by the adapter.

seams.name: WebSocketServer synchronized(this) stop coordination and single-start latch
seams.note: Server lifecycle only.
seams.rust_mapping: Server adapter run-once guard and join-on-shutdown.

seams.name: synchronized(connections) registry and broadcast frame cache
seams.note: Registry of live connections with snapshot-copy-before-iterate. Broadcast's per-draft frame cache (doBroadcast/fillFrames, 1052-1104) shares one Framedata across connections in Java.
seams.rust_mapping: Server adapter owns the registry; broadcast becomes iterate + per-connection command enqueue sharing only immutable bytes (Arc) to keep the no-shared-mutable-state premise.

seams.name: SSLSocketChannel synchronized read/write
seams.note: TLS channels are outside the Sans-I/O core and the thin TCP adapters of US-018; listed for census completeness.
seams.rust_mapping: None (out of scope).

seams.name: SSLSocketChannel2 synchronized processHandshake/wrap/unwrap
seams.note: Out of port scope, same rationale as L7; delegated-task executor is seam T7.
seams.rust_mapping: None (out of scope).

seams.name: WebSocketImpl.readyState (the only volatile in the connection core)
seams.note: Written inside L2 methods and open(); read without any lock by decode, the state getters, the send gate, the client read loop, and the flush path. Permits check-then-act races (see race.send_vs_close).
seams.rust_mapping: State is owned by the single owner; commands arriving after close initiation get a typed rejection; any external ready_state() snapshot is an advisory atomic load. The Java race window is not part of the deterministic behavior corpus.

seams.name: WebSocketImpl.flushandclosestate
seams.note: Written only under L2 (592); read without the monitor by eot() and isFlushAndClose() from the selector thread. A JMM data race, benign in practice; drives server-side close-once-outQueue-drains.
seams.rust_mapping: A plain field of the owner's state: the flush path is an owner action, so the read is naturally ordered.

seams.name: WebSocketImpl.lastPong
seams.note: Unsynchronized 64-bit read/write between the decode thread (PONG processing, open()) and the connectionLostChecker thread; formally racy in Java.
seams.rust_mapping: Adapter keeps the timestamp updated from a PongObserved event emitted by the owner.

seams.name: WebSocketImpl.closecode/closemessage/closedremotely
seams.note: Written under L2 in flushAndClose; read by the no-argument closeConnection and eot(), ordered in practice by the flushandclosestate latch protocol; the triple is delivered verbatim in the terminal event.
seams.rust_mapping: Fields of the owner's Closing state variant: impossible to read before set, by type.

seams.name: WebSocketImpl.tmpHandshakeBytes
seams.note: Decode-thread handshake accumulation buffer, nulled inside synchronized close (504) while decodeHandshake may be mid-use: a genuine Java race window (incidental as a race, load-bearing as buffering semantics; see race.handshake_buffer_vs_close).
seams.rust_mapping: Handshake buffer owned by the owner; close command and inbound bytes are serialized, so the race is structurally absent; buffering and limit semantics ported exactly (US-005 handshake corpus).

seams.name: Draft_6455 decoder state vs draft.reset()
seams.note: incompleteframe/currentContinuousFrame/extension/protocol are decode-thread state, but reset() runs from whatever thread initiates close, racing an in-flight translateFrame/processFrame (see race.reset_vs_decode). Load-bearing in aggregate: post-close frame processing must stop and reassembly state must drop.
seams.rust_mapping: Reset is an owner-internal effect of the close transition; inbound bytes after the close transition are handled by the state machine (decode gated on OPEN, WebSocketImpl.java:227-232).

seams.name: WebSocketClient lifecycle fields (socket/ostream/writeThread/connectReadThread/engine)
seams.note: Mutated across connect()/run()/reset()/onWebsocketClose with interrupt+join as the sync points.
seams.rust_mapping: Client adapter owns the socket and two tasks (reader, flusher) joined on shutdown; reconnect rebuilds them.

seams.name: WebSocketImpl.key/channel/workerThread
seams.note: NIO plumbing set by the selector thread and read by L2 closeConnection from arbitrary closing threads.
seams.rust_mapping: The adapters own the socket handle; ConnectionCore never sees it (Sans-I/O).

seams.name: WebSocketImpl.outQueue (unbounded LinkedBlockingQueue)
seams.note: FIFO order is wire order; write-then-onWriteDemand is the flush trigger; unboundedness means Java has NO send backpressure; the queue is cleared wholesale on CancelledKeyException, silently dropping enqueued writes at close.
seams.rust_mapping: Bounded command/write queues with a typed QUEUE_FULL_REJECTED outcome (divergence.bounded-command-queue) and a typed DROPPED_ON_CLOSE outcome (divergence.silent-drop-on-close); committed writes preserved in order.

seams.name: WebSocketImpl.inQueue
seams.note: Server-only in practice (selector produces, pinned worker consumes; the client decodes directly on its read thread). Load-bearing for ordering only: arrival order equals decode order; the queue mechanism itself is incidental.
seams.rust_mapping: The owner consumes inbound bytes directly as BytesIn actions in arrival order.

seams.name: WebSocketServer.buffers pool + queuesize ceiling
seams.note: Read-buffer pool for the NIO adapter; the selector thread blocks when the pool is empty, an implicit global inbound backpressure mechanism that is emergent Java behavior.
seams.rust_mapping: The blocking adapter (US-018) gets explicit bounded read-buffer accounting instead; an adapter-level behavior consideration, not core.

seams.name: WebSocketWorker.iqueue with per-connection worker pinning
seams.note: Pinning each connection to exactly one worker serializes per-connection decode while allowing cross-connection parallelism. Load-bearing as an invariant (per-connection frame processing serialized in arrival order; callbacks for one connection never run concurrently); incidental as a mechanism.
seams.rust_mapping: The single owner IS the serialization; cross-connection parallelism is one owner task per connection.

seams.name: WebSocketServer.iqueue (List, selector-thread-only)
seams.note: Wrapped-channel re-read list, single-threaded and largely SSL-specific.
seams.rust_mapping: None needed; adapter-internal.

seams.name: WebSocketServer.isclosed AtomicBoolean
seams.note: Shutdown semantics are observable: stop is idempotent, in-flight close handshakes get a bounded window, and late connections are refused with GOING_AWAY.
seams.rust_mapping: Server adapter shutdown gate mirroring the same observable semantics (GOING_AWAY for late handshakes).

seams.name: WebSocketServer.queuesize AtomicInteger
seams.note: Buffer-pool ceiling arithmetic; incidental beyond the adapter.
seams.rust_mapping: Adapter-internal accounting.

seams.name: NamedThreadFactory.threadNumber AtomicInteger
seams.note: Thread naming only; the migration map routes the seam to US-017 as the study-surface thread seam.
seams.rust_mapping: Thread/task naming in the adapters.

seams.name: WebSocketClient.connectLatch
seams.note: Counted down on BOTH open and close so connectBlocking returns false on failed connects instead of hanging; blocking-connect semantics including the failure path are observable.
seams.rust_mapping: Oneshot completed by the first Open-or-Terminal event.

seams.name: WebSocketClient.closeLatch
seams.note: Counted down on close; awaited by closeBlocking.
seams.rust_mapping: Oneshot completed by the terminal event.

seams.name: Server selector thread
seams.note: Owns socket I/O, outQueue drain, the buffer pool, eot on EOF, and server-role close-on-flush. Boundary events: onWriteDemand from any sender sets OP_WRITE and wakes the selector (server/WebSocketServer.java:848-857).
seams.rust_mapping: Flush task; server-side close-after-drain becomes an owner-scheduled effect.

seams.name: WebSocketWorker pool (decode + user callbacks)
seams.note: Each worker runs decode -> processFrame -> user callbacks; callback thread identity and per-connection callback serialization are observable to user code; the uncaught-throwable path closes the connection.
seams.rust_mapping: Owner task delivers events to the delivery sink in order; callback serialization holds by construction.

seams.name: connectionLostChecker scheduled thread
seams.note: Per-tick snapshot + sendPing or abnormal closeConnection: a third mutator of connection state concurrent with the selector/worker and user threads (see race.timer_vs_worker).
seams.rust_mapping: Adapter timer emits Ping / abnormal-close commands through the owner queue.

seams.name: Client connectReadThread
seams.note: Socket setup, sendHandshake, then the read/decode loop ending in eot().
seams.rust_mapping: Client adapter reader task.

seams.name: Client WebsocketWriteThread
seams.note: outQueue.take loop with interrupt-drain, then closeSocket in finally: socket teardown is the write thread's job, triggered by interrupt.
seams.rust_mapping: Shutdown command drains committed writes, then the adapter closes the socket.

seams.name: User caller threads (send*/close/broadcast/sendPing)
seams.note: Any thread may call the send/close surface: these are the multiple producers of US-017 AC1.
seams.rust_mapping: N producers enqueue typed commands onto the bounded MPSC queue.

seams.name: SSL delegated-task executor
seams.note: Out of port scope with L7/L8.
seams.rust_mapping: None (out of scope).

fairness.subject: action.outbound_flush
fairness.rationale: While writes are pending the flusher eventually runs: mirrors the selector's OP_WRITE re-arm plus wakeup loop. Model counterpart: WF_vars(FlushWrite) in connection-model.tla.

fairness.subject: owner command/inbound processing
fairness.rationale: The pinned worker always returns to its take loop, so queued per-connection work is eventually processed; the port's owner task must not park while commands or inbound actions are queued.

fairness.subject: closing resolution (peer close, close-on-drain, or transport EOF)
fairness.rationale: A closing connection eventually terminates. Model counterpart: WF_vars(ResolveClosing) in connection-model.tla, checked by the ClosingLeadsToClosed property.

fairness.subject: admission ordering among competing producer tasks
fairness.rationale: Deliberately absent. Java's unbounded LinkedBlockingQueue provides no admission fairness among competing senders, and the port declares none: no producer is guaranteed admission ahead of another, and systematic schedules MUST include producer-starvation orderings. Asserting fairness here would be an unfounded strengthening over both Java and the port design.

races_not_corpus_encodable.racy_java_behavior: A send can pass the isOpen gate while another thread enters CLOSING; the enqueued frame is then either flushed before the close frame's queue position or silently dropped when the key is cancelled.
races_not_corpus_encodable.why_not_corpus_encodable: The outcome depends on the JMM interleaving of an unsynchronized volatile check-then-act, not on any deterministic function of the input byte/action sequence; Java-fidelity is defined over serialized observable event sequences, not racy interleavings.
races_not_corpus_encodable.deterministic_rust_semantics: The owner serializes commands against transitions: commands committed before close-initiate are flushed in order; commands arriving after receive TYPED_REJECTION_POST_CLOSE.

races_not_corpus_encodable.racy_java_behavior: draft.reset() runs from whatever thread initiates close, racing an in-flight translateFrame/processFrame on the decode thread; mid-decode state clearing is indeterminate.
races_not_corpus_encodable.why_not_corpus_encodable: The observable result depends on where the decode thread is preempted inside translateFrame; no input sequence pins it.
races_not_corpus_encodable.deterministic_rust_semantics: Reset is an owner-internal effect of the close transition; close commands and inbound bytes are serialized, so the race is structurally absent and post-close input is handled by the state machine.

races_not_corpus_encodable.racy_java_behavior: The connectionLostChecker thread's abnormal closeConnection runs concurrently with worker decode and user sends; whether a message callback or the abnormal terminal event wins is timing-dependent.
races_not_corpus_encodable.why_not_corpus_encodable: Wall-clock timer firing cannot be expressed as a deterministic input action against the pinned runtime.
races_not_corpus_encodable.deterministic_rust_semantics: The adapter timer emits Ping/abnormal-close commands through the owner queue; their order relative to other commands is the queue order, which schedules enumerate explicitly.

races_not_corpus_encodable.racy_java_behavior: A local close and a peer close race to the CLOSING transition; the L2 monitor makes the losing path a no-op.
races_not_corpus_encodable.why_not_corpus_encodable: Which side wins is an interleaving property; the corpus can encode either serialized order but not the race itself.
races_not_corpus_encodable.deterministic_rust_semantics: The owner applies whichever close arrives first in the serialized order; the second becomes IDEMPOTENT_NOOP_ALREADY_CLOSING (US-017 lists simultaneous close explicitly).

races_not_corpus_encodable.racy_java_behavior: close() nulls tmpHandshakeBytes inside the L2 monitor (504) while the decode thread's decodeHandshake may be mid-use of the same buffer (248-264), which decodeHandshake reads and reassigns without any lock: mid-handshake close can produce an NPE on the decode thread or silently drop accumulated handshake bytes, depending on the preemption point.
races_not_corpus_encodable.why_not_corpus_encodable: The outcome depends on where the decode thread is preempted inside decodeHandshake relative to the closing thread's null-out; no deterministic input byte/action sequence pins that interleaving, so the corpus can encode either serialized order but not the race itself.
races_not_corpus_encodable.deterministic_rust_semantics: The handshake buffer is owned by the single owner; close commands and inbound bytes are serialized, so the race is structurally absent, while the buffering and limit semantics are ported exactly (US-005 handshake corpus).

races_not_corpus_encodable.racy_java_behavior: onWriteDemand hitting CancelledKeyException clears outQueue wholesale: writes enqueued around close are silently discarded.
races_not_corpus_encodable.why_not_corpus_encodable: Whether a write lands before or after key cancellation is scheduler-determined.
races_not_corpus_encodable.deterministic_rust_semantics: Committed writes are either flushed before terminal teardown or reported with a typed DROPPED_ON_CLOSE outcome; silence is not an outcome.

SCOPE: this append_state governs THIS PLAN'S two planned port-vs-Java deltas below, only them. They remain unappended: the ledger's aggregate READY gate (internal/lab VerifyBaselineEvidence) requires the build/adapter/tests/Autobahn baselines PASS; the Autobahn baseline is BLOCKED (0/247 both modes, NO_FURTHER_RERUNS_AUTHORIZED), so ledger status stays BLOCKED_PENDING_BASELINE and the two appends stay planned, and MUST be executed against the ledger if that baseline lands. Fabricating executed-observation digests to force their append is the decorative-evidence pattern US-006 review discipline blocks.

SEPARATELY, the ledger now carries 59 divergence records (head above). Composition: 32 Java-vs-RFC records under the owner AC-amendment decision of 2026-08-27 (us010-016-ac-amendment-owner-decision-2026-08-27.json, sha256 26849b5e..., making ledgering every recorded Java-vs-RFC emulation divergence mandatory before US-010..016 acceptance); two E5b Autobahn follow-ups (delta-c5429efb close-echo wire composition, Autobahn 7.3.2; delta-71c02bf6 dispatch-phase echo enqueue, Autobahn 5.15); delta-9dd3ab86 under the owner rejected-close-transition decision (sha256 d7a54e2c...): the ordered port change was implemented, measured the public corpus down to 73/74 against the LIVE Java transcript, fired that decision's own escape clause, and was reverted, so the divergence is recorded not coded; sequences 36-48 below; sequence 49, the C6 protocol-violation close reaction (delta-5b996412) under us017-c6-layer-split-owner-decision-2026-08-28.json (sha256 d41b5307...), appended LAST at the claude/post-failure landing so nothing before it moves; and sequences 50-56, seven records held for want of a disposition vocabulary, now supplied by document schema 1.2.0.

SEQUENCES 36-44 close the acceptance audit's ledger gaps G3c/G3d/G3e (drafts/acceptance/ROLLUP.md). G3c was a missing DIRECTION: all sixteen original handshake records cite client_request cases, the SERVER slice, leaving the CLIENT-handshake direction zero coverage while evidence/us005-handshake-live-mapping.json recorded six divergent server_response rows; sequences 36-41 are those six. Sequence 42 ledgers the Transfer-Encoding smuggling seed. Sequence 43 ledgers the pre-open refusal-recoverability divergence, whose direction is the unusual one: the port is STRICTER than Java, a port-vs-Java safe strengthening. Sequence 44 records a reserved-bit rejection leaving ReadyState OPEN, flagged by the cross-plane defect audit (drafts/codex-us020-defect-crosscheck.md section 8), confirmed unledgered by a saturating re-check of all 35 prior records.

REVIEW ROUND 2 (session 01a0464f) found several of those preimages bound WRONG RFC readings: worse than a citation slip, the preimage being hashed and therefore load-bearing evidence. Every reading was re-verified against the authoritative RFC text; the reviewer upheld on every substantive point. The three client-handshake BUDGET records were rebuilt as safe-strengthening records: RFC 6455 mandates no handshake size, header-count or header-line limit anywhere, so the port ADDS a bound rather than emulating a leniency. THAT ROUND'S OWN BASIS WAS CORRECTED IN TURN (review 01a0495e, BLOCKING 9): it quoted as verbatim section 10.4 a MAY-implement-limits sentence appearing nowhere in RFC 6455, and called the section purely permissive. The real 10.4 places a MUST on an implementation with frame-size or reassembled-message-size limitations and a SHOULD on imposing frame and message limits. The conclusion stands on SCOPE rather than modality (10.4 is about frames and reassembled messages, never the opening handshake), and all six affected records now quote it verbatim in full from one shared constant so the copies cannot drift. The bare-LF record was rebuilt because RFC 9112 section 2.2 expressly PERMITS recognizing a bare LF as a line terminator, making Java's refusal conformant. The duplicate-header record was rebuilt because RFC 9110 section 5.3 permits comma-combination and binds the SENDER, not the recipient; the Transfer-Encoding record moved onto RFC 9112 section 6.3's MUST 400 rather than section 6.1's SHOULD 501. The Content-Length record was WITHDRAWN: Content-Length: 0 is a valid zero-length body, documenting a divergence that does not exist.

SEQUENCES 45-47 supersede FROZEN sequences 14, 15 and 16, carrying that same wrong section-10.4 basis in the server-side budget records for us005.hs.0046/0047/0048. Correcting them in place would rewrite the chain from sequence 14, so protected/ledger-frozen-prefix-owner-decision-2026-08-28.json (sha256 bb3cd0da7f4aed014290dab3dc35b2ec87f41d3d7e7a8c7449816159e9d837c7, recomputed by internal/deltaledger.VerifyCitedOwnerDecisions whenever the protected store is reachable) ruled SUPERSEDE, DO NOT REWRITE, on the immutable-store sidecar pattern this plane used for the US-009 handoff corrections and attempt-0128 sandbox reconciliation. Each superseding record names the sequence it corrects, quotes the wrong basis verbatim, binds the verified correct basis, and reclasses the divergence a SAFE STRENGTHENING. The superseded records stay in the chain with digests intact, so the error stays visible beside its correction.

SEQUENCE 48 is the protocol-rejection-readystate CLASS record. Sweeping the public corpus BY CAUSE (expected.error.code JAVA_INVALID_DATA, the decoder's typed rejection, raised on a `bytes` step derived by EXECUTING the scenario, never from expected.counts, with final_state open) matches EIGHTEEN scenarios across ten families, all caused by the oracle adapter never routing through WebSocketImpl.decodeFrames; the hand audit found roughly a twentieth of the class. The earlier sweep selected on close_code in {1002,1007,1009}, a RESULT SHAPE, wrongly enrolling us005.pub.0000: a locally initiated send_close(999) with zero inbound bytes, which RFC 6455 section 7.1.7 does not require closing and sequence 35 ledgers correctly (review 01a0495e, BLOCKING 4). The class is enumerated mechanically in evidence/us005-public-rfc-divergence-census.json, every row must name a ledger record whose hashed preimages discuss that scenario.

INTEGRITY OF THIS FIELD'S SIBLING: unledgered_disagreements was a fake gate, schema-pinned const 0 and hardcoded in build.go, its only real detector never fed a committed observation set. It read clean while G3c and the reserved-bit proposition were unledgered. It is now COMPUTED and the readiness gate refuses on nonzero. THE FIRST VERSION OF THAT FIX WAS CIRCULAR (review 01a0495e, BLOCKING 1): observations were built one-per-definition, so 1:1 with the records by construction, and the count could only move if a record was DELETED; a newly observed divergence nobody had written down, the G3c failure, still read zero, reproduced by execution before being fixed. The measurement now has TWO ARMS: a digest arm comparing the committed observation set against the chain, and an EVIDENCE arm sweeping the committed live handshake mapping and the public corpus for any divergence no record is about. Both are assigned in one place, internal/deltaledger.BuildLedgerFileFrom, which the polarity tests drive rather than setting the field (BLOCKING 2). The censuses moved out of _test.go files into internal/deltaledger production code, run inside cmd/deltaledgerctl --check which rust/Makefile invokes from gates via ledger-gates; they were assertions in a test binary no release path ran (BLOCKING 3). Coverage is semantic on both sides (BLOCKING 5, 6); supersession is a machine-visible SUPERSEDES token in each correction's hashed rationale, rendered to evidence/java/ledger-supersessions.json (BLOCKING 8).

None of this changes the committed 35-record prefix, which stays byte-identical with sequences 14, 15, 16 and 35 all keeping their digests, nor 36-49: the new class field is OPTIONAL. planned_deltas.java_behavior: outQueue is an unbounded LinkedBlockingQueue: every send is admitted and there is no send backpressure of any kind.
planned_deltas.port_behavior: Bounded command/write queues sized by the bounds block; admission failure is the typed QUEUE_FULL_REJECTED outcome instead of unbounded memory growth.
planned_deltas.rationale: Deliberate divergence: unbounded admission is a resource-exhaustion hazard the port does not reproduce. The observable delta (a producer can see QUEUE_FULL_REJECTED where Java would accept) must be ledgered before any conformance run that could observe it.

planned_deltas.java_behavior: CancelledKeyException in onWriteDemand clears outQueue wholesale: writes enqueued around close are silently discarded with no signal to the sender.
planned_deltas.port_behavior: Writes not flushed before terminal teardown are reported with a typed DROPPED_ON_CLOSE outcome per write; nothing is discarded silently.
planned_deltas.rationale: Deliberate divergence: silent loss is replaced by a typed outcome. The delta is observable to instrumented senders and must be ledgered before any conformance run that could observe it.
